faq.a: An IPO, or Initial Public Offering, is when a private company first offers its shares to the public to raise capital, allowing ordinary investors to buy a piece of the company.
The "issue price" is the fixed price at which a company offers its shares to investors during its IPO.
A "listing gain" is the percentage increase from the IPO issue price to the price at which the shares open for trading on the stock exchange on their first day.

faq.q: What does "return vs. IPO price" mean?
faq.a: This metric shows how much the current share price has changed, in percentage terms, compared to the original IPO issue price. It tells you the overall gain or loss from the IPO price to now.

faq.q: What is an anchor investor lock-in?
faq.a: An "anchor investor lock-in" is a period (often 30 or 90 days) during which large institutional investors, who bought shares before the main IPO, are restricted from selling their shares in the open market.
